index.summary: The Jackson City Council continued deliberation on the FY2026-2027 municipal budget, which must be passed by September 15. The council approved several amendments shifting funds toward police and fire, including $438,000 more for JPD and $156,000 more for fire personnel, while reducing Public Works, Planning, Administration, General Government, and IT personnel lines. The total general fund budget stands at $113,250,961. The council did not vote on final passage, recessing until Friday at 10 a.m. to allow legal review of bond documents before potentially reducing the city's reserve to fund additional fire and police hires.

topics.title: Emergency addition: JPD FY2025-2026 budget revision
topics.note: Council added an emergency item to revise JPD's current-year budget for a grant-funded transfer needed to purchase brass tracks; passed.

topics.title: FY2026-2027 budget introduced
topics.note: Resolution approving and adopting the municipal budget for FY2026-2027 was moved and seconded; deliberation began.

topics.title: Budget deadline and total
topics.note: CFO Caldwell said revenues are projected at about $113.5 million; total all-funds budget is $337,348,801, with general fund at $113,250,961.

topics.title: Revenue actuals dispute
topics.note: Councilwoman Clay questioned why FY2024-25 actuals were shown instead of FY2025-26; staff said only about $100 million collected so far with $10-12 million expected in September.

topics.title: Parking fines and court revenue
topics.note: Councilman Foote questioned $20,000 vehicle parking fines and $100,000 misdemeanor fines; staff said these are court-collected estimates.

topics.title: Sales tax projection
topics.note: Pro-rata state sales tax projected at $31,969,801 for FY2025-26; staff said $25.4 million collected through 11 months with $1.6 million expected in September.

topics.title: Thalia Mara Hall rent zeroed out
topics.note: Councilman Foote objected to $0 rent projection for Thalia Mara Hall; CAO said revenue may go to a separate account under the Convention Center management agreement.

topics.title: Interest income estimate
topics.note: Councilman Foote said $1.5 million interest estimate is too low given 2.6% rate and ~$85 million average balance; CAO defended conservative estimate.

topics.title: Public Works funding streams
topics.note: Discussion that Public Works receives general fund, 1% sales tax, bond, modernization, and state/federal funds; general fund proposed at $19.7 million.

topics.title: Amendment: shift $250,000 from Public Works to JPD
topics.note: Councilman Parkinson moved to reduce Public Works personnel services to $8,837,480 and increase JPD other services and charges to $1,728,262; passed 3-0-1.

topics.title: Amendment: move $70,000 from CAO office to fire
topics.note: Motion to reduce general government personnel services to $5,362,934 and increase fire personnel services to $24,171,517; passed 4-0.

topics.title: Proposed consolidation of HR, IT, constituent services, communications
topics.note: Councilman Foote proposed merging departments; motion withdrawn for lack of second, to be revisited after budget.

topics.title: Amendment: shift $122,000 from Planning to police and fire
topics.note: Motion to reduce Planning personnel services to $3,982,870, increase JPD other services to $1,828,262, and fire personnel to $24,193,517; passed 3-0-1.

topics.title: Amendment: shift $90,000 from Administration to fire and police
topics.note: Motion to reduce Administration personnel services to $3,156,433, increase fire personnel to $24,226,571, and JPD other services to $1,885,262; passed.

topics.title: Amendment: eliminate IT BSA position, split savings
topics.note: Motion to reduce IT personnel services to $1,841,345, increase fire personnel to $24,257,571, and JPD other services to $1,916,262; passed 4-0.

topics.title: Public Works wages and contracts
topics.note: Director Anderson said lowest Public Works salaries are $22,000; council asked him to review contracts for possible raises.

topics.title: Thalia Mara Hall and zero revenue lines
topics.note: Council pressed CAO to review Thalia Mara Hall agreement and other zeroed revenue lines; CAO agreed to review.

topics.title: Recess to next day
topics.note: Meeting recessed until the following day at 3 p.m. to continue budget deliberation.

topics.title: Updated budget totals after amendments
topics.note: CFO Caldwell summarized amendments: JPD total $33,432,200; fire $25,529,736; Public Works $19,459,502; Planning $8,146,467; Administration $4,170,391; General Government $15,569,088; IT $1,882,759; general fund total $113,250,961.

topics.title: Motion to move housing programs to Mayor's office
topics.note: Councilman Foote moved to move HUD-funded housing programs from Planning to Mayor's office; passed 6-0.

topics.title: Fire department staffing and ISO rating
topics.note: Chief Thomas said 25 additional firefighters per year needed to reach 112 per shift for ISO rating; cost is about $1.6 million for 25 hires.

topics.title: COPS grant eligibility discussion
topics.note: JPD grants manager said city cannot apply for COPS hiring grants unless budgeted officer positions are filled; past grant had repayment issues.

topics.title: Reserve fund proposal for fire and police
topics.note: Councilman Stokes proposed reducing reserve from 7.5% to 5% to fund fire and police; CAO warned bond documents may require maintaining reserve level.

topics.title: Legal review of bond documents
topics.note: City Attorney Moncure said legal will review bond documents by end of week to see if reserve reduction could trigger debt acceleration.

topics.title: Contract review request
topics.note: Councilman Foote asked legal to review contracts including garbage, parking meters, Smith-Wills, and Thalia Mara for fair revenue terms.

topics.title: Grand Gulf emergency planning funds
topics.note: Councilman Foote noted $600,410 in Grand Gulf emergency planning fund could be used for one-time expenses; CAO agreed.

topics.title: Grove Park insurance proceeds
topics.note: Councilman Foote noted $2,499,508 in insurance proceeds from 2013 hail storm; CAO said funds are being spent on Grove Park improvements.

topics.title: Recess until Friday
topics.note: Council recessed until Friday at 10 a.m. for final budget vote after legal review.
